title: Underlined Text

illustrates.quote: Print Font Attributes UEB defines symbols for italics, bold, underlining, and script. There are also five transcriber-defined typeform indicators to be used for other print font attributes. Each typeform indicator requires the addition of a symbol, word, or passage indicator. Passage indicators require the use of a typeform terminator. (See Formats, Appendix G, for a list of these symbols and UEB, §9, Typeforms.) See Sample 5-1: Underlined Text, page 5-14.

blocks.features: Braille-only transcriber's note (opened/closed by '@.<'...'@.>') defining a single-underline word indicator and a double-underline word indicator; no counterpart in this Sample's own print excerpt.
White bold text reversed out of a solid maroon/dark-red banner; a recurring textbook feature heading, not specific to this exercise.
Exercise number '15-40.' bold (blue); instruction text plain.
items: **15–40.** Write the twenty-six prepositional phrases in this part of an encyclopedia entry. Underline each preposition once and its object twice.

blocks.text: **Example:** Cultured pearls come in a variety of colors.
blocks.features: Bold label 'Example:' followed by a plain demonstration sentence.

A worked demonstration line placed directly beneath the example sentence, underlining the two prepositional phrases: each preposition ('in', 'of') is singly underlined (standard UEB underline-word indicator), and each object ('variety', 'colors') is doubly underlined (the sample's one transcriber-defined symbol, reused for both).

print.notes: This numbered Sample begins at line 7 of the braille excerpt given in the source (lines 1-6 absent, not invented). Cross-referenced from rule 5.1.4 ('See Sample 5-1: Underlined Text, page 5-14'); illustrates needing both a single-underline (word) indicator and a double-underline (word) indicator for the same general attribute at two intensities, matching 5.1.4's point that each typeform indicator needs a symbol/word/passage form.
print.surroundingText: Cross-referenced from rule 5.1.4; this is the exercise that rule illustrates.

resolution: Braille re-derived independently from .txt lines 4261-4276 (field width 5); matches run A's rendering, which correctly preserves the genuine 4/6/2-cell runover indents run B stripped (the same section-wide bug documented elsewhere). `lineNumbers` (run B's own schema addition, not in the original task-brief schema) is adopted here since the source itself prints an explicit line number on every line of the three numbered Samples — a genuinely present structural fact worth preserving separately from `lines`.
